# Rules reference

All 21 content rules and 11 spec checks in GTM Toolkit, with the reasoning, default severity and options for each one.

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-docs.mjs from `gtm reference`. Do not edit by hand. -->

GTM Toolkit 2.0.0 ships 21 content rules, run by `gtm lint`, and 11 spec checks, run by `gtm validate`.

Set a rule to `error`, `warn` or `off` in `gtm.yaml`, and pass options as a second value:

```yaml
lint:
  rules:
    seo/title-length: [warn, { min: 30, max: 60 }]
    messaging/untagged: error
```

## SEO and structure

What search engines, screen readers and language models need from the shape of a page.

### seo/title

Every page has a title in its frontmatter.

The title becomes the <title> tag, the search result headline and the link text in llms.txt. A page without one is invisible everywhere at once.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/title-length

Titles fit the space search results give them.

Search engines cut titles at roughly 60 characters. Very short titles waste the most valuable line you own.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page · Options: `{"min":20,"max":65}`

### seo/description

Every page has a description (or summary) in its frontmatter.

The description is the meta description, the social card text and the one sentence an assistant reads in llms.txt before deciding whether to fetch the page.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/description-length

Descriptions are long enough to say something and short enough to survive truncation.

Search results show about 160 characters. Past that the sentence is cut mid-thought; far below it you are leaving the pitch to the crawler.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page · Options: `{"min":70,"max":160}`

### seo/date

Articles carry a real date in YYYY-MM-DD form.

The date feeds the sitemap lastmod, the Article structured data and the ordering in llms.txt. A date that does not parse silently drops the page out of all three.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article

### seo/slug

URLs are lowercase words separated by hyphens.

Mixed case and underscores produce duplicate URLs and links that break when someone retypes them. Changing a live URL needs a redirect, so catch it before publishing.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/single-h1

The frontmatter title is the only H1.

The page template renders the title as the H1. A second "# Heading" in the body gives the page two competing subjects.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/heading-order

Headings do not skip levels.

Screen readers, search engines and language models all use the heading tree as the outline of the page. An H2 followed by an H4 is a hole in the outline.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/image-alt

Images have alt text.

Alt text is what a blind reader hears, what an image search indexes and all a text-only model ever sees of your chart.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/link-text

Link text says where the link goes.

Anchor text is how crawlers and assistants learn what the target page is about. "Click here" teaches them nothing, and neither does a pasted URL.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/internal-links

Internal links and images point at something that exists.

A link to a page that 404s wastes the click and the crawl. The toolkit knows every URL the site serves, so it can check before a reader does.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/min-internal-links

Articles link to at least one other page on the site.

An article with no internal links is a dead end for readers and an orphan for crawlers. One relevant link is the smallest unit of a content strategy.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article · Options: `{"min":1}`

### seo/placeholder

No placeholder text or links ship.

Drafts leak. A leftover task marker, filler text or a link to "#" in production tells readers nobody read the page before it went out. Code blocks are ignored.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/markdown-fence

Code fences are closed.

An unclosed fence turns the rest of the page into one grey code block. It is the most common way a post breaks in production.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/unique-title

No two pages share a title.

Two pages with one title compete for the same query and are indistinguishable in a sitemap, a search result or an llms.txt index.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### seo/unique-description

No two pages share a description.

A copied description usually means a copied page template. Each page deserves its own pitch.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

## Messaging

What the page says, checked against the strategy in your spec.

### messaging/avoid

Content does not use terms the messaging spec rules out.

Every team has words it decided not to use: a competitor's framing, a retired product name, a house style rule. Writing them down once in messaging.vocabulary.avoid means people and agents both get corrected before review, not during it.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### messaging/prefer

Content uses the preferred spelling of the terms the team owns.

If the site says "GTM as code", "GTM-as-Code" and "go to market as code", search engines and language models see three weak terms instead of one strong one. Consistency is how a phrase becomes yours.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### messaging/refs

Frontmatter personas, topics and pillars exist in the spec.

Tagging a post with a persona that was renamed last quarter quietly removes it from every coverage report. References are checked like imports.

Default: `error` · Applies to: article, doc, page

### messaging/topic-keywords

A page tagged with a topic uses that topic's language up front.

The topic file is the keyword source of truth. If a page claims a topic but its title, description and opening never use one of the topic's phrases, either the tag or the page is wrong.

Default: `warn` · Applies to: article, doc, page · Options: `{"words":150}`

### messaging/untagged

Articles declare the topic or persona they serve.

Content with no topic and no persona cannot be counted in `gtm coverage`. Off by default, because a new spec starts with a backlog of untagged posts; turn it on once the backlog is cleared.

Default: `off` · Applies to: article

## Spec checks

These run on the `gtm/` files themselves and are not configurable.

| Check | Severity | What it catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec/yaml-syntax` | error | A spec file is not valid YAML. |
| `spec/schema` | error | A value is missing, misspelled or of the wrong type. |
| `spec/duplicate-section` | error | A section is declared both inline and in its own file. |
| `spec/duplicate-id` | error | Two personas, pillars, topics, differentiators or competitors share an id. |
| `spec/unknown-ref` | error | A persona or pillar id is referenced but never declared. |
| `spec/collection-path` | error | A content collection points at a directory that does not exist. |
| `spec/unproven-claim` | warn | A pillar or differentiator makes a claim with no proof attached. |
| `spec/persona-questions` | warn | A persona lists no questions, so there is nothing to answer for them. |
| `spec/unused-persona` | warn | A persona is declared but no positioning, pillar or topic targets it. |
| `spec/length` | warn | A one-liner or short boilerplate is too long for the places it gets reused. |
| `spec/own-vocabulary` | warn | The spec itself uses a term its vocabulary says to avoid. |
